expectations.text: Base URL 是 https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/plan/v3 且使用 Agent Plan 专属 Key
expectations.evidence: review_compare.py L40 `DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding/v3"`; L140-145 reads generic `ARK_API_KEY` described as 'your Volcengine Ark API key' with no mention of the Agent Plan dedicated key. NOTES.md L11 calls /api/coding/v3 'the endpoint Ark uses for the subscription (Agent/Coding Plan) models' and offers /api/v3 as the only alternative; /api/plan/v3 is never mentioned. Real behaviour (verification A2): Agent Plan key on /api/coding/v3 → 401 `{"error":{"code":"AuthenticationError","message":"The API key or AK/SK in the request is missing or invalid. ..."}}`. Every request in the script fails.

expectations.text: 对 kimi-k3 限长用的是 max_completion_tokens（或明确说明 max_tokens 会把思维链算进去而预留了远大于 300 的额度），不会出现 max_tokens=300 导致空回答
expectations.evidence: L163 `max_tokens=max_tokens` with `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 300` (L41) for both models; `max_completion_tokens` is never used. NOTES.md L25 does acknowledge 'hidden reasoning tokens are counted inside max_tokens, so if Kimi thinks at length the visible answer can be shortened or cut', but the script keeps 300 and only prints a `[warn]` after the fact (L215-216). Real behaviour (verification C7): kimi-k3 with max_tokens=64 → finish_reason length, content "", reasoning 61; with max_tokens=300 the reasoning budget is still far too small for a code review, so an empty or truncated answer is the expected outcome. The assertion's escape clause requires reserving a budget far above 300, which was not done.

expectations.text: glm-5.3 关闭思维链没有使用 thinking: {type: disabled}（真实返回 400 thinking.type disabled is not supported by this model），而是 reasoning_effort=low 之类被接受的取值
expectations.evidence: L104-109 glm-5.3 ModelSpec: `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}`; NOTES.md L24 calls this 'Ark's request-level switch for turning chain-of-thought off on reasoning-capable models'. Real behaviour (verification C2): glm-5.3 + thinking.type=disabled → 400 `{"error":{"code":"InvalidParameter","message":"thinking.type `disabled` is not supported by this model ..."}}`. reasoning_effort is not used anywhere. The glm-5.3 half of the comparison can never succeed.

expectations.text: 没有使用 reasoning_effort=none（真实返回 400）
expectations.evidence: grep for `reasoning_effort` in review_compare.py and NOTES.md returns nothing; the script never sends the parameter in any form. Passes literally, but only because a different (also rejected) mechanism was chosen — see assertion 3.

expectations.text: 从 message.reasoning_content 与 message.content 分别取思维链与正文，而不是假设思维链混在 content 里
expectations.evidence: L180 `result.content = (msg.content or "").strip()`; L181-182 comment 'Ark returns chain-of-thought (when enabled) as a non-standard `reasoning_content` field' and `result.reasoning_content = getattr(msg, "reasoning_content", None)`; L189-191 reads `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. print_report L217-219 reports reasoning_content length separately from the answer.

claims.claim: /api/coding/v3 is the endpoint Ark uses for subscription (Agent/Coding Plan) models addressed by plain model name
claims.evidence: Conflates Coding Plan and Agent Plan. Verification A2: Agent Plan key on /api/coding/v3 → 401 AuthenticationError. Agent Plan's entry is /api/plan/v3 (A3 → 200).

claims.claim: thinking: {type: disabled} is Ark's request-level switch to turn off chain-of-thought on reasoning-capable models; with it, glm-5.3 spends the whole 300-token budget on the answer and returns no reasoning_content
claims.evidence: Verification C2: glm-5.3 rejects it with 400 `thinking.type `disabled` is not supported by this model`. The switch works on doubao-seed-2.0-lite (C5) but not on glm-5.3; the only accepted way is reasoning_effort=low (C3).

claims.claim: On Ark, hidden reasoning tokens are counted inside max_tokens
claims.evidence: Partially true: correct for kimi-k3 (C7), false for doubao-seed-2.0-lite where max_tokens does not cap the chain of thought (C6). The claim is stated but not acted upon — the default stays at max_tokens=300.

claims.claim: If thinking is rejected for a model the SDK raises APIError, which the script catches and prints per model without aborting the other
claims.evidence: L167-170 catches APIError and stores the message; main() continues to the next spec. However this means the glm-5.3 review is always an [ERROR] line, so the requested comparison is never produced.

claims.claim: Adding the same thinking: disabled flag to kimi-k3 is a valid one-line fix if Kimi's answer gets cut
claims.evidence: kimi-k3 + thinking.disabled was not tested in verification-findings.md; cannot be confirmed. Given kimi-k3 supports max_completion_tokens (C7), the documented fix is the wrong lever.

claims.claim: No API calls were made while writing this
claims.evidence: NOTES.md L33 'Not verified' section states this explicitly.

uncertainties: NOTES.md L33: parameter names come from Ark's public OpenAI-compatible API docs and were not verified against the real API; author acknowledges `thinking` might be rejected for a given model.
NOTES.md L11: unsure whether the user's plan lives under /api/coding/v3 or /api/v3; /api/plan/v3 not considered.
needs_review: Default endpoint + key type will 401 for an Agent Plan user; the glm-5.3 request will 400 even on the correct endpoint; kimi-k3 at max_tokens=300 will likely return empty/truncated content.
workarounds: Relies on prompt structure (~200 words) plus a post-hoc finish_reason==length warning instead of reserving reasoning budget.

suggestions.assertion: 没有使用 reasoning_effort=none（真实返回 400）
suggestions.reason: This run passes it trivially by never using reasoning_effort at all while sending an equally rejected thinking.disabled. Merge into assertion 3 so the check is 'uses an accepted mechanism' rather than 'avoids one specific bad value'.

No assertion checks that the script can actually deliver the requested comparison end-to-end (both reviews non-empty). Here the per-model error catching lets the script 'succeed' at printing while producing zero usable reviews; an assertion like 'both models are expected to return non-empty content under the chosen parameters' would name that outcome directly.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-3 are strongly discriminating and caught three real production failures. Assertion 4 is trivial; an end-to-end 'comparison actually produced' assertion is missing.
